newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria Bradys swing with repayment rumours.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Bradys swing with repayment rumours.

text.p: Bulgarian debt prices slumped in early Tuesday trading only to recover as rumours swung back and forth over whether the government had honoured its debt servicing payments.
Bulgaria was due to pay $135.5 million today to service its Brady debt and had earmarked money to do so.
Several traders said they had heard reports of a delay in the payment but believed it to be only a technical matter.
"It's nonsense. Somebody wanted to hit the market and buy the stuff. (Technical delays) happen all the time. This doesn't mean anything. I'm not worried," one U.S. bank trader said.
Bulgarian IABs had slipped close to a point but later recovered much of their lost ground.
There was no immediate word from the Bulgarian government or the Euroclear settlement agency on the fate of the payments.
However, the Bulgarian government some time ago said it had set aside the money from a reconstruction and development fund.

The volatility of the Brady price shows how seriously investors view the possibility of default by Bulgaria as it makes little headway in dragging itself out of political and economic chaos, one trader said.

Bulgaria was widely expected to be able to meet today's payment but many analysts believe default is still on the cards later this year unless an agreement can be struck in time with the International Monetary Fund.
The rest of the market, which has dipped this week, was very quiet.
One European bank trader said that Russia, though, was still looking a bit soft following the recent bout of profit-taking.
